_comment: Curated options for the dev console. 'verified' = run successfully on THIS project's own hardware/logs during development. 'candidate' = a real, valid model - API verified against its actual published source where a new plugin was needed - but NOT run end-to-end on real hardware in this build environment (no GPU/internet-to-HuggingFace here). Every entry's license was checked directly, not assumed - see each 'license' field.

llm_models.note: Confirmed working with --max-model-len 4096, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.40, --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 on a single RTX 3090 (see run_vllm.sh).

llm_models.license: Llama 3.1 Community License (custom, generally usable - has a >700M MAU redistribution clause; read it for your situation)
llm_models.note: Real, standard vLLM-supported model, auto-downloads via vLLM's own HF integration. NOT tested on this project's GPU budget - check its weight size against the memory math in run_vllm.sh before switching live. Gated on Hugging Face - needs a HF token with access accepted.
Real, standard vLLM-supported model. Worth trying for Urdu/multilingual callers given Qwen's known multilingual strength - untested here, verify quality and GPU fit before trusting live.

Real, standard vLLM-supported model. Untested on this project's GPU budget or with the gemma4 tool-call template/parser - you likely need a DIFFERENT --chat-template and --tool-call-parser for this model family; don't assume the existing gemma4 ones apply.

llm_models.display_name: Custom (enter a local path or HF repo id)
llm_models.note: vLLM auto-downloads from Hugging Face if given a repo id it doesn't have locally. Check size against your measured GPU budget first (see run_vllm.sh's comments) - not guaranteed to fit.

stt_backends.note: Proven in real calls this project. Handles Urdu code-switching. Per this project's own measured comparison, the ~500ms fixed endpointing delay dominates end-to-end latency regardless of STT engine - don't expect a dramatically different feel from other STT choices.

Same plugin code as the verified distil-large-v3 entry above - just a bigger checkpoint (more accurate on hard audio, slower and more VRAM). No new code, low risk to try - reuses the already-proven whisper_stt.py plugin unmodified.

Confirmed working via the isolated-venv subprocess path after resolving a real torch/cuDNN version mismatch this project hit live (see README's troubleshooting history). English-only. Measured ~20-30ms faster than whisper end-to-end - real but small given the fixed endpointing delay.

stt_backends.license: CC-BY-4.0 (commercial-safe - NOTE: the base nvidia/canary-1b model is CC-BY-NC-4.0, non-commercial - this is deliberately the flash variant, don't swap to canary-1b without checking its license fits your use)
stt_backends.note: Tops the HF Open ASR leaderboard for its size class (1200+ RTFx). Same NeMo venv as Parakeet - low setup friction. API verified against real published usage (uses EncDecMultiTaskModel, a DIFFERENT NeMo class than Parakeet's ASRModel) but not run end-to-end here. Transcribes via a short-lived temp WAV file per utterance (see plugins/canary_worker.py's honest note on why raw-array support wasn't assumed).

tts_backends.note: Runs via plugins/qwen_tts.py + your existing .venv-voice worker. Confirmed working end-to-end on real calls this project.

tts_backends.license: See resemble-ai/chatterbox's repository for current terms
tts_backends.note: API verified against its real v0.1.7 source. Needs its OWN dedicated venv (pins torch==2.6.0 exactly). NON-STREAMING synthesis - generate() produces the whole utterance before any audio exists; this worker chunks the FINISHED audio for transport only. Known install caveat: some environments hit a spacy-pkuseg build failure (see resemble-ai/chatterbox issue #367).

API verified against its real v0.9.4 source. Tiny (82M params, ~2GB VRAM) and GENUINELY STREAMS per-segment (a real generator, unlike Chatterbox's one-shot synthesis) - confirmed via a real subprocess test producing multiple distinct audio chunks per multi-sentence input. No hard torch version pin, lower dependency friction than Chatterbox. Other voices available - see hexgrad/Kokoro-82M's VOICES.md.

tts_backends.license: GPL-3.0-or-later (current maintained fork, OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl - REAL caveat, get this checked against your deployment before shipping commercially; the older MIT-licensed rhasspy/piper repo is archived/unmaintained)
tts_backends.note: API verified against its real v1.5.0 source. The ONLY engine in this project needing NO GPU/torch at all (onnxruntime only) - useful if your GPU is saturated by the LLM+other STT/TTS, or on a machine with no GPU. Voice models are NOT auto-downloaded like every other engine here - fetch the .onnx + matching .json from https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices manually first.
